light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a ranch hand with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the kitchen behind stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores and uneven tone; hair with stray curls; the denim shirt faded and creased, the leather apron scuffed. Food looks like real home cooking, not styled. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld video filmed by a ranch hand with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the kitchen in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and rough working hands; he moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

clips.text: Step four. How do you know when they're done? Here's a trick most people get wrong. They fish out one bean, taste it, and it's soft, and they turn off the pot. And then half the beans in the bowl are still chalky.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, holds up the spoon with one bean, then shakes his head. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: Beans don't all cook at the same speed. Some are older, some are bigger. So you take five beans. Not one. Five. Blow on them, and bite each one.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, counts five beans into his palm from the spoon and blows on them. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: They should all be creamy all the way through, with no white chalky dot in the middle. If even one of them is chalky, give it fifteen more minutes and test five more.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, bites one bean in half and looks closely at the inside. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps.
